intervals.label: COUPP-60 commissioning and engineering run at Fermilab (MINOS near-detector hall)
intervals.note: No start date is published: arXiv:1008.3518 (submitted August 2010) says the 60 kg COUPP chamber 'is being commissioned'; the March 2012 dissertation says it 'recently completed a successful engineering run at the MINOS near detector hall at Fermilab' (Appendix D). Fermilab news (2017): 'after extensive testing, the detector was moved to SNOLAB in 2012'.
intervals.quote: At the time of this writing, a 60 kg CF3 I COUPP bubble chamber is being commissioned.

intervals.label: installation and commissioning at SNOLAB
intervals.note: Move to SNOLAB in 2012 (Fermilab news). The dissertation expected data taking 'near the end of 2012'; the CosPA 2013 abstract says the chamber 'began operating in summer 2013', and the first PICO-60 run dates from June 2013.
intervals.quote: Work began at Fermilab in 2005, and, after extensive testing, the detector was moved to SNOLAB in 2012.

intervals.label: run 1 (CF3I)
intervals.quote: We report results from the first run of PICO-60, with a dark matter exposure of 3415 kg-days taken at SNOLAB between June 2013 and May 2014.

intervals.label: refurbishment (data taking suspended)
intervals.locator: PICO-60 page (Internet Archive capture of 5 July 2026)
intervals.note: 'Between the summer of 2014 and 2016': the detector was upgraded, cleaned and refurbished.
intervals.quote: Between the summer of 2014 and 2016, data taking was suspended to allow the PICO-60 detector to be upgraded, cleaned, and refurbished.

intervals.label: run 2 (C3F8)
intervals.note: Data taking resumed in 2016 (month not given); the C3F8 blind exposures were taken November 2016-January 2017 and April-June 2017 (arXiv:1702.07666, arXiv:1902.04031).
intervals.quote: Data taking resumed in 2016, but for run 2 the target was filled with C3F8 to improve the sensitivity to spin dependent dark matter interactions.

intervals.label: decommissioned
intervals.quote: PICO-60 was decommissioned after the end of the data taking in the summer of 2017.

intervals.label: C3F8 first blind exposure (1167 kg-days at 3.3 keV)
intervals.quote: of 1167 kg-days, taken between November 2016 and January 2017.

intervals.label: C3F8 second blind exposure (1404 kg-days at 2.45 keV)
intervals.quote: a second blind exposure was acquired between April and June 2017 at a threshold of 2.45 keV

placements.note: Engineering run of the COUPP-60 chamber in the MINOS near-detector hall at Fermilab (Fermilab surface campus point).
placements.quote: The COUPP 60 kg bubble chamber recently completed a successful engineering run at the MINOS near detector hall at Fermilab.

placements.note: Ladder Labs area of SNOLAB, in a water tank; the site record is the single SNOLAB underground-lab point. Start is the 2012 move (Fermilab news); end is the 2017 decommissioning.
placements.quote: The pressure vessel is located in a 2.9-m-diameter by 3.7-m-tall water tank in the Ladder Labs area of SNOLAB [15].

depth.quote: Located at SNOLAB: 6800 ft depth (6010 m.w.e.), one of the deepest labs

exposure.quote: A new blind 1404-kg-day exposure at 2.45 keV threshold was acquired with approximately the same expected total background rate as the previous 1167-kg-day exposure at 3.3 keV.

target_mass.quote: a bubble chamber filled with 52 kg of C$_3$F$_8$ located in the SNOLAB underground laboratory

target_medium.quote: a bubble chamber filled with 52 kg of C$_3$F$_8$

threshold.quote: The chamber was operated at thermodynamic thresholds as low as 1.2 keV without loss of stability.

summary.plain: A 30-cm-wide, 1-m-tall silica jar of superheated liquid (CF3I, then C3F8) in a water tank, watched by cameras and microphones for the tell-tale bubble of a dark matter collision.
summary.technical: 30-cm-diameter by 1-m-long synthetic fused-silica bell jar sealed to a stainless-steel bellows, hydraulic fluid (propylene glycol), water buffer above the target, two (run 1) then more (run 2) cameras, piezoelectric sensors; 60 cm by 167 cm pressure vessel in a 2.9 m by 3.7 m water tank.

technology.quote: The PICO-60 bubble chamber consists of a 30-cm-diameter by 1-m-long synthetic fused silica bell jar sealed to a flexible stainless-steel bellows and immersed in hydraulic fluid
technology.value: Superheated bubble chamber (CF3I, later C3F8) in a synthetic fused-silica jar with water buffer, stereoscopic cameras and piezoelectric acoustic sensors
